298-**Notes, edit & delete**
299-
300:- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to attach a note using lightweight Markdown (bold, italics, lists, links) to a bookmark.
301-- **FR-015**: Users MUST be able to edit a bookmark's title, description, address, note, and tags.
302-- **FR-016**: Users MUST be able to permanently delete a bookmark, with a confirmation step before removal.
--
305-
306-- **FR-017**: System MUST provide case-insensitive search across titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses.
307:- **FR-018**: Search MUST support `#tag` terms that restrict results to a given tag, and MUST combine ordinary text with `#tag` terms conjunctively so both conditions must hold.
308:- **FR-019**: Search MUST support exact-phrase matching via quotes, and MUST treat operator words placed inside quotes (e.g. `"AND"`) as literal search text rather than boolean instructions.
309-- **FR-020**: Search MUST support boolean combinations using AND, OR, NOT and parentheses for grouping.

332-**Saved copies**
333-
334:- **FR-030**: Users MUST be able to keep a saved local copy of a bookmarked page as a self-contained local HTML file that can be reopened later.
335-- **FR-031**: When a bookmarked address points to a PDF, System MUST store the PDF file itself as the saved copy instead of an HTML snapshot.
336-- **FR-032**: Users MUST be able to request preservation through the Internet Archive; System MUST record the resulting archive reference on success and report failure clearly without losing the bookmark.
--
338-**Import & export**
339-
340:- **FR-033**: Users MUST be able to export the collection to a standard browser-bookmark HTML file that preserves each bookmark's title, tags, and original date added alongside its address.
341:- **FR-034**: Users MUST be able to import a standard browser-bookmark HTML file, preserving each bookmark's title, tags, and original date added (mapping folder labels to tags where present) and avoiding duplicates of already-saved addresses.

343-**General**
--
350-- **Tag**: A short user-defined label grouping bookmarks. Many-to-many with bookmarks.
351-- **Saved Search**: A stored query combining search text with included and excluded tags, rerunnable by the user.
352:- **Saved Copy**: A preserved version of a bookmarked page — a self-contained local HTML file, a stored PDF file, or an Internet Archive reference — associated with a bookmark.
353-- **Preferences**: The user's display settings: default sort order, number of items shown, and text size.
354-
--
364-- **SC-006**: A user can apply an action (tag, mark read/unread, archive, or delete) to at least 50 selected bookmarks in a single operation.
365-- **SC-007**: A user can archive and later restore a bookmark with no loss of its data, tags, notes, or saved copies.
366:- **SC-008**: Exporting and then re-importing a collection preserves 100% of bookmark addresses, titles, tags, and original dates added, without creating duplicates.
367-
368-## Assumptions
--
373-- **Automatic page information requires network access**: Collecting title/description/icon/preview and keeping saved copies require fetching the live page; when a page is unreachable, the app degrades gracefully (FR-006) rather than failing the save.
374-- **Internet Archive is an external dependency**: Preservation through the Internet Archive relies on that third-party service; when it is unavailable the local copy and bookmark are unaffected and the failure is reported honestly.
375:- **Simple note formatting**: Notes use lightweight Markdown — bold, italics, lists, and links — rather than a full rich-document editor (confirmed with client).
376-- **English-language UI**: A single-language interface is sufficient for v1.
